evidence: Nirvana performed 'The Man Who Sold the World' (1970) on MTV Unplugged in New York, recorded November 1993 and broadcast and released in 1994; Cobain named it as one of his favorite Bowie songs in interviews around the taping.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Bowie's original is glam-adjacent art rock with a clean, almost detached vocal. Nirvana's version, acoustic guitars and Cobain's rawer, more strained voice, turns the same melody considerably more haunted, recorded only months before his death.

explanation: Nirvana covered David Bowie's 'The Man Who Sold the World' on MTV Unplugged in 1993, released in 1994. Many listeners only learned it was a cover afterward, since Nirvana's version became better known than Bowie's original to a new generation who mostly knew Nirvana rather than glam rock. It was recorded months before Cobain's death, and that timing has shaped how it is heard since.
